project: Ghoztty session persistence — build + thorough E2E test
userIntent: Build the hybrid local-agent session persistence (design doc §5) and prove it: simulate a binary upgrade where every window reloads intact — correct positions/splits, same screen buffers, processes still running (re-attached, NOT restarted). Test thoroughly, not just build.

loop: 1. On session start: read THIS file fully, then the design-doc sections referenced by the task you pick. Do not re-explore the codebase for facts already in keyFacts below.
2. Pick the first task with status=pending whose dependsOn are all done. Set it to in_progress (edit this file) before starting work.
3. Do the task. Keep it small; if it balloons, split it into sub-tasks in this file and finish only the first.

4. Verify per the task's acceptance. Build must pass; run the named tests. For user-facing changes, kill + relaunch the DEBUG app from this worktree and verify live (never while the user has live debug windows you did not create).

5. Commit on this branch: git add -A && git commit with a descriptive message ending in the Claude Co-Authored-By trailer. Record the SHA + outcome + surprises in the task's notes, set status=done (or blocked with reason).
6. Add any newly-discovered follow-up tasks to the tasks array (small, ordered).

7. If tasks remain: invoke the Skill tool with skill='dzearing-skills:reset-context' and args='Read /Users/dzearing/git/ghoztty-session-persistence/docs/design/session-persistence-tasks.json and follow its protocol: execute the next pending task, then reset context again.' — this clears context and re-seeds the next session.
8. If ALL tasks are done (or only blocked ones remain): do NOT reset. Write a final summary for the user: what shipped, E2E results, what is blocked and why.
rules: NEVER touch /Applications/Ghoztty.app in any way — it is the user's primary terminal. Debug app only: zig-out/Ghoztty-Debug.app (bundle id com.dzearing.ghoztty.debug, socket ghostty-debug-<uid>.sock).
All bundle identifiers stay in com.dzearing.ghoztty.* — NEVER com.mitchellh.*.
NEVER run +new-remote-window unattended against a possibly-unreachable host: a failed dial pops a modal alert that wedges ALL CLI IPC. Loopback dials to an agent you just health-checked are OK.
Use /usr/bin/log (never bare `log` — zsh builtin shadows it).
A `kill -STOP`ed process gets pending teardown signals delivered at SIGCONT — run freeze/thaw cycles in one tool call.

Stale-instance trap: after rebuilding, verify the debug app process start time > binary mtime before trusting live behavior. Kill any debug instance launched from other/deleted worktrees first (the user's real terminal is the RELEASE app; killing DEBUG instances is safe unless this effort created live test windows).
Agent test seam: GHOSTTY_AGENT_LOCK=<path> GHOSTTY_AGENT_HEARTBEAT=<path> lets a test agent run beside any real one. Agent flag is --listen=127.0.0.1:<port> (there is no --port flag).

+split --name= on remote/agent-backed windows registers the pane ASYNCHRONOUSLY since T04 (onCreate callback after the cwd RPC; loopback ≈ ms, real remote = latency-bound) — poll briefly before using the name, or use +list to discover panes.
If the user interrupts with new instructions, encode them as tasks in this file instead of drifting.

NEVER 'tell process "ghoztty"' by NAME in System Events — the RELEASE app has the same process name and it WILL be targeted (this created a tab in the user's real terminal once). Scope by pid ('first process whose unix id is N') or better: use the app's own AppleScript interface via 'tell application id "com.dzearing.ghoztty.debug"'.

Driving tabs headlessly: the scripting interface (new tab / close tab / select tab / windows / tabs) works even while the SCREEN IS LOCKED; AX menu-bar clicks do NOT (zero AX windows exposed, action silently no-ops). 'new tab in (first window whose id is "tab-group-…")' — ids match +list. Known wart: 'new tab' errors -10000 even on success (T06d); re-discover the pane via +list.
Screen locked also means the KEYCHAIN is locked — relay-account loads can block for minutes (observed 185s, off-main).
Do not kill -9 + relaunch the app with <2s gap until T06b is fixed: the restore probe races the agent's dead-peer detection and DESTROYS manifest entries for live sessions.

environment.cli: zig-out/Ghoztty-Debug.app/Contents/MacOS/ghoztty +<action> … (or the ghoztty binary inside the debug bundle); debug socket is separate from release
environment.notes: Official zig 0.15.2 binary cannot link on this macOS 26.4 box; the brew zig@0.15 bottle works (see memory ghoztty-macos26-zig-toolchain).

decisions: Direction: design doc §5 hybrid — local ghoztty-agent owns PTYs; viewer keeps a layout+sessionId manifest; agent later gains disk metadata for reboot floor. User approved 2026-07-13 ('let's try it').
v0 local transport = loopback TCP (both ends already exist: agent --listen, ghostty_remote_connection_new_tcp). Unix-socket + peercred is a hardening task AFTER the headline E2E works (T09).
session-persistence is an opt-in config flag initially (default off) so the debug app stays usable throughout.
Ring stays 2 MB default for the demo; configurable size + 16 MB default comes with T11.
Reboot recovery (agent disk persistence, RELAUNCH) comes after the upgrade demo (T12/T13) — the upgrade scenario keeps the agent alive, so it does not need disk persistence.

headlineAcceptance.scenario: Simulated binary upgrade (what the user asked to prove)
criteria: Setup: >=2 windows, >=4 panes total with nontrivial split topology and distinct ratios, each pane running `echo PANE=<n> PID=$$; i=0; while true; do echo tick-<n>-$((i++)); sleep 1; done` (unique markers).
Action: capture +list --json snapshot; quit/SIGKILL the app; REPLACE the debug app bundle with a freshly-built one (simulating Sparkle swap); launch the new binary.

Pass: every pane's shell/child PID unchanged and process never exited (tick counter continued monotonically across the gap — no reset to 0); split tree (directions, ratios ±0.01), window count, titles match the snapshot; +read on each pane shows pre-kill scrollback lines (replayed) AND post-gap ticks; time from kill to all panes interactive < 10 s.

tasks.notes: 2026-07-14: done, commit 3e3f355a0. FILE store (not UserDefaults): ~/Library/Application Support/<bundle-id>/session-layout.json, atomic tmp+rename, file deleted when last entry removed. IPCServer gained registeredWindowName(forController:)/registeredPaneName(forSurface:) (nil when unnamed); AppDelegate.ipcServer now private(set). 10 new Swift Testing tests + full GhosttyTests bundle pass. tasks.title: Restore at launch: rebuild windows + splits, re-attach every leaf
tasks.goal: At app launch (flag on), replay the manifest: recreate each window at its frame, rebuild the SplitTree with exact directions/ratios, each leaf a .remote surface with its recorded sessionID (agent replays ring → scrollback restored), restore titles/ipc names.
steps: Model on restoreRemoteWindows() (AppDelegate.swift:1365) + presentRemoteWindow(sessionID:), extended to multi-leaf trees: construct SplitTree nodes directly (native, exact ratios — do NOT shell out to +split/+rearrange).
Dead/not_found sessions: leaf shows exited state (reuse childExited overlay or a banner); do not crash the tree build.

Interplay: persistent windows must NOT also be restored by AppKit TerminalRestorable (avoid double windows) — gate restorable off for agent-backed windows like explicit-command windows already do (TerminalController.swift:69-74).

tasks.notes: 2026-07-14: done, commit 6c6e32b64. Entry point AppDelegate.restoreSessionLayoutWindows (new SessionLayoutRestore.swift), called from applicationDidFinishLaunching !isTestHost, gated on flag. Flow: set hasPendingSessionRestore (suppresses initial launch window; cleared + fallback initial window if restore ends empty) → LocalAgentManager.sharedConnectionAsync (new non-blocking API, warmUp now wraps it) → bg thread probes every leaf session (query_cwd_timeout 5s) → main thread groups entries by tabGroupID/tabIndex → per entry SplitTree via SessionLayoutManifest.makeTreeNode (new pure inverse of encodeNode; +leaves(of:) pairs views/manifest leaves by tree order) with per-leaf ATTACH cfg → controller ADOPTS entry.id (set BEFORE remoteConnection so didSet skips duplicate registration; entry never drained — crash-safe) → frame setFrame AFTER showWindow (showWindow re-applies defaults) → titleOverride → registerRestoredRemoteWindow + new IPCServer.registerRestoredPane → syncAndCaptureSessionIDs. Drop policy: nil tree dropped; ALL leaves dead/uncaptured dropped; agent unreachable keeps everything; partial death restores (dead leaves attach-fail to exited overlay). LIVE VERIFIED: 3 windows/6 panes across 5 kill -9 cycles + 1 graceful quit + 1 binary-swap relaunch (rebuild → kill → new binary re-attached = upgrade primitive); nested vert+horiz topology exact; +rearrange'd ratio 0.31 restored exactly; titles, ipc names (+send-keys/+read post-restore) OK; ticker PID 96130 monotonic to 841 across every gap; scrollback replayed. HARD-WON GOTCHA (AppKit dupes): windowDidLoad-only isRestorable gate FAILS — the window loads DURING TerminalController.init (surface-tree observer touches self.window) before any entry id binds; unified log proved layoutEntry=nil at every windowDidLoad. Fix = 3 gates: windowDidLoad check + BaseTerminalController.disableAppKitRestorationForSessionLayout (called from registerSessionLayoutIfNeeded AND restore path; guards isWindowLoaded to avoid forcing nib load) + willEncodeRestorableState guard (backstop). macOS 26: ~/Library/'Saved Application State' does NOT exist (unknown location); stale PRE-fix snapshots multiplied on every kill-9 relaunch (11 dupes at peak) because kill-9 replays whatever snapshot exists; purge = +close dupes then GRACEFUL quit (rewrites state) then relaunch. Discovered +rearrange --layout JSON (ratio 10-90 %) — T07 can use it for distinct ratios. UNTESTED: tab-group restore path (no CLI creates tabs → T06a). Fixture left: app RUNNING (current build, launched --session-persistence=true --confirm-close-surface=false) with 3 restored windows; agent 18770 owns the sessions.

tasks.notes: 2026-07-14: done, incl. tasks.title: Restore drop-policy is destructive on probe failure (+ fast-relaunch poisoned connection)
tasks.goal: SEEN LIVE: kill -9 the app and relaunch ~1s later → LocalAgentManager dial reports ready, but ALL query_cwd probes return empty within ~2ms (agent still had the dead app's bridges bound) → restore treated every session as gone and REMOVED all manifest entries (layout permanently lost) even though every shell was alive under agent 18770. Worse, that instance's shared connection stayed poisoned: EVERY subsequent ghostty_surface_new failed ('surface error view will render', session=-) until the app was restarted. Make the drop policy conservative and the connection resilient.
steps: SessionLayoutRestore.probeSessions: distinguish 'agent says dead/not_found' from 'probe failed/empty' (query_cwd empty ≠ dead — needs an RPC that returns session status; T10's LIST_SESSIONS is the natural fix, or probe retry with backoff).
Drop policy: only remove a manifest entry on POSITIVE dead; on inconclusive probes keep the entry and skip (or retry) — losing layout on a race is worse than a stale entry.

Investigate the poisoned shared connection: after the failed probe pass, all surface_new calls failed for the process lifetime (repro was one-off; log evidence at 2026-07-14 20:39:56, pid 29256). Suspect agent-side single-bridge state after abrupt viewer death + instant redial; possibly interacts with locked-keychain relay-account load (185s hang observed).
E2E guard: T07's harness should use >=2s gap OR the fix should make 0s gaps safe (agent must detect dead TCP peer promptly — RST arrives immediately on kill -9).
tasks.acceptance: kill -9 → instant relaunch (no sleep) restores every window reliably 3x in a row; no manifest entry is ever removed while its agent session is alive; test-agent still passes.
tasks.notes: 2026-07-15: done. ROOT CAUSE of the destruction: the restore liveness probe inferred 'session alive' from GET_CWD returning a non-empty cwd. During a fast relaunch the agent still had the dead app's bridge bound, so the child cwd read failed → empty reply → EVERY session read as dead → all entries removed, though the sessions were alive in the agent's table. FIX (three layers): (1) Protocol: CWD reply gains additive `found: ?bool` — the agent sets it from `getByIdStr(session_id) != null`, i.e. TABLE PRESENCE, which is independent of whether the child/bridge cwd read succeeds. This is the real cure: existence is now answered from the store, not inferred from cwd. Older agents omit the field. (2) Client: new Connection.probeSessionTimeout → tri-state {alive,dead,unknown}: ok=true OR found=true ⇒ alive; found=false ⇒ POSITIVE dead; timeout/malformed/old-agent(found=nil) ⇒ unknown. Exported as ghostty_remote_connection_probe_session (c_int 1/0/-1) in embedded.zig + ghostty.h. (3) Swift drop policy (SessionLayoutRestore): probeSessions now returns [sessionID: .alive/.dead/.unknown]; an entry is forgotten ONLY when EVERY leaf is POSITIVELY .dead — .unknown or missing-id leaves keep the entry AND rebuild+attach it (a live session re-attaches; a truly-gone one shows its exited overlay but the layout survives to retry next launch). BONUS crash-safety: SurfaceView now stashes expectedRemoteSessionID from its creation config, and manifest sync falls back to it when the live id is unavailable (e.g. ghostty_surface_new failed) so a failed-restore sync can't blank a recorded id. Also added an @errorReturnTrace() dump on the ghostty_surface_new failure path (the 'poisoned connection' OutOfMemory) so a recurrence attributes the failing `try` — see below. COMMIT: cda38f18f. Zig: 5 new probeSession connection tests (all pass, 90/90 connection.zig), 2 agent GET_CWD tests extended to assert `found` (test-agent exit 0). LIVE VERIFIED with a FRESH new-binary agent (pid 480): fixture = 3 persistent windows (initial + winA 2-pane split + winB), 4 sessions, tickers A0/A1/B0 PIDs 1405/1926/2553. Ran kill-9 + INSTANT relaunch (0s gap) x3: every cycle restored 3/3 windows, agent pid unchanged, all 4 session ids preserved, no PANE= reprint (no ticker reset — B0 monotonic 51→73), and ALL THREE shell PIDs still alive parented to agent 480 afterward. Zero 'error initializing surface' / 'surface error view' in the log across all cycles. Suspects: session ring/offset state reset on clean DETACH or on force=true reclaim (attached_elsewhere retry in Remote.zig:280); snapshotOffset()==0 skipping the gap-fill; ring writes gated while a (dead) bridge is still bound.

tasks.acceptance: After both graceful-quit and kill -9 relaunch, +read on every restored pane shows pre-gap scrollback AND the output produced during the gap; test-agent passes with new coverage.
tasks.notes: 2026-07-15: done. ROOT CAUSE was NOT agent-side (the ATTACH gap-fill at server.zig:784-816 was correct) — it was a CLIENT-side registration RACE. The client uses TWO separate reader threads over TWO independent streams (connection.zig: control_thread + data_thread, `control`/`data` Streams). On ATTACH the agent frames ATTACHED on the CONTROL lane and the whole ring replay as DATA on the DATA lane. The client only calls channels.register(ch) AFTER the control-lane ATTACHED reply unblocks the caller (connection.zig:1597, attachChannelCancellable). Because the two lanes have NO cross-stream ordering, the data thread frequently ran routeInboundData for the replay DATA BEFORE register() completed → ChannelTable.pushTo found no channel → returned .unknown → bytes DROPPED (inbound_ring.zig old line 388). Microsecond race → per-pane coin-flip, exactly the 'same agent, same cycle, different panes' symptom. Fresh OPEN-new rarely bit because a new shell emits no output for ~ms; ATTACH replay dumps the ring instantly. FIX (client-only, additive): ChannelTable gained a bounded pre-registration buffer `pending: map<channel, ArrayList(u8)>`. pushTo now BUFFERS bytes for a not-yet-registered channel (new RouteResult variant `.buffered`) instead of dropping; register() FLUSHES pending[ch.id] into the ring under the SAME mutex right after map.put, so buffered (pre-register) bytes always precede live (post-register) bytes and none are lost — atomic vs. concurrent pushTo. Bounds: max_pending_bytes_per_channel=256KiB (one client ring), max_pending_channels=16 (hostile-input cap); over-cap excess dropped (old behavior); deregister/deinit free un-claimed buffers. connection.zig routeInboundData treats `.buffered` like `.unknown` (no FLOW). Since real ATTACH always sends last_byte_offset=0 (Remote.zig:264, resync_active=false), no resync-trim interaction; test_client resync path pre-registers so never buffers. This ALSO closes the same latent race for OPEN-new. COMMIT: 4337a9c23. TESTS: inbound_ring standalone 11/11 (3 new: in-order flush T06c, per-channel byte cap, channel-count cap); connection.zig 93/93 (was 90); zig build test-agent exit 0; full app build OK. LIVE E2E (fresh fixture: 2 windows / 4 panes A0/A1/B0/B1, each a unique `echo PANE=n PID=$$; while true tick` loop, agent pid 43438, shells 43441/45205/45448/45688): ran 3x kill -9 + INSTANT (0s) relaunch AND 1x graceful AppleScript quit + relaunch. EVERY cycle, ALL 4 panes replayed pre-gap scrollback (oldest replayed tick well before the pre-kill anchor), ZERO PANE= reprints (no shell restart), tick counters monotonic across the gap (76→104→130→148→175→177 no reset), agent pid + all 4 child PIDs unchanged throughout. 4/4 panes consistent on all 4 cycles = the intermittency is gone. Fixture LEFT RUNNING (app relaunched, agent 43438) for T07. NOTE: unnamed leaf panes (B0) get a NEW auto-registered UUID name each restore (explicit --name like B1/A1 persist) — the T07 harness must re-discover unnamed panes via +list after each relaunch (it already plans to). Also confirmed T06b fast-relaunch safety holds under my change (0s-gap restores never lost a window).
